correctness.rationale: Every positive extinction orbit eventually satisfies x_(n+1)<=rho*x_n and y_(n+1)<=rho*x_n for q<rho<1. Therefore x_n,y_n are summable exponentially. C1 regularity implies the weighted series sum (j+1)|log(f(x_j)/q)-a*y_j|<infinity, while the analytic term log((exp(a*y_j)-1)/(a*y_j)) is summable. Exact logarithmic telescoping proves x_n/(Cq^n)->1 and y_n/[D(aC)^n q^{n(n+1)/2}]->1 for positive finite C,D. The Ricker below-Allee region is invariant and geometrically contracting, giving a nonempty unconditional domain. Threshold times follow from logarithm inversion and eventual monotonicity. The actual standalone verify.py was executed and returned VERIFY_OK in three settings; all infinite-time steps rest on the analytic proof.

residual_risks: A generic unindexed theorem for superstable noninvertible ecological maps could encode this asymptotic by abstraction; semantic searches are evidence, not a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: A source-motivated biological collapse basin has two mathematically distinct first-detection clocks: plant biomass reaches small thresholds after logarithmically many generations but herbivore biomass after square-root-logarithmically many. The universally sharp rb/2 exponent and full nonzero orbit constants distinguish biological timescales invisible to origin eigenvalues and prior qualitative extinction. The result covers every positive extinction trajectory and proves a C1 shared-biomass structural mechanism rather than simply evaluating a numerical example or renaming a known invariant.
